posts.title: Davejsp's Technic Creations
posts.text: <- Back to Index of Davejsp's Technic MOCs thread 42099 Wild Beast This is one of my B-Models for the LEGO Techncic set 42099 4x4 X-treme Off-Roader. This "Wild Beast" MOC has a gear ratio of 1:1.67 and I bet you're asking if it can run at all, like, it shouldn't have enough torque to drag its weight around... Chapter 1: Planning for speed Things I knew from the start that had to be implemented: -Using the set's planetary wheels hub was out of the question. -To reach a gear ratio higher than 1:1, gears had to be used. The MOC needed to be RWD only and the two XL motors dedicated to the two rear wheels with the transmission being as simple and short as possible to avoid friction, and the gears couldn't be in a perpendicular setup to avoid loss of efficiency. -If the MOC was going to be fast, I would need to steer with precision, to help with that, I wanted the front axle to have a positive caster angle. -Being fast means it also needs a sturdy chassis, so, for this MOC in particular, I would be using as many pieces as necessary to make the chassis as robust as possible and make it impossible for the structure to disassemble while running. -Some kind of suspension was necessary, but at this point, I still wasn't sure what direction I would take; I didn't want to use independent suspension on all wheels to avoid complexity (and possibly more friction) though, but something simpler. Chapter 2: Chassis When it comes to RC MOCs, I almost always start by designing the chassis and making the electric components an integral part of it. Since this would be an original MOC and not a replica of anything, I was free to do whatever I wanted, in the end, I just wanted something with an aerodynamic aesthetic. Rear axle I started with the rear axle, using the set's differential was not an option because it would require gears in a perpendicular setup and it's just not efficient; I took some time to decide between having both XL motors driving a solid axle, or the two XL motors driving one rear wheel each, independently, I went with the second option mostly because a solid axle would create a lot of stress when steering and slow down the MOC a lot. Then it went through several redesigns because the prototype rear axle was too wide, I ended up using a solid structure with an unconventional, asymmetric design for the rear axle. Front axle Before starting to design the front axle, I had to decide what kind of suspension the MOC would have. Since I wanted to focus on steering precision and the rear axle was a solid structure, I decided to implement live axle suspension on the rear axle only. Without suspension at the front, the build required much less complexity, this allowed me to create a very simple and solid front axle, with a positive caster angle, which helps the steering align naturally on its own. Chassis The next step was to connect both the front axle and rear axle to a center structure containing the hub and test the hell out of it for sturdiness; a turntable was used to implement the live axle suspension at the rear. Then I created a profile on the Powered Up app and drove the chassis around like crazy, oh man, was it fast... I wish I had some footage of that. Chapter 3: Modelling Now that I have a functioning chassis, I need to give it shape, as I mentioned before, I didn't have a specific idea, I just wanted something aerodynamic, probably some kind of buggy, so I started experimenting with the set's panels. It didn't take much time for me to start forming an overall shape in my head and start working towards it. I started with the front, aggressive-looking headlights, and low profile; and built the dash and basic interior; for the rear bodywork, I tried to make it look somehow curvy to be consistent with the rest of the design. posts.text: That's pretty much the premise of The Marvels: "Carol's a bad friend, family member, and even enemy and needs to mend her ways." It comes off more like the writers, through Monica and others, berating her for not fitting their preferred mould of "overtly emotional female character obsessed with motherhood" while desperately dressing her up in girly frills (all the singing, dancing, and romancing a prince - she even somehow changes her Starforcer suit into a dress for that!). There's some other stuff as well in this supposedly feminist Marvel movie (admittedly an oxymoron). Like Fury lording it over all three of our heroines (the same Fury that was little more than Carol's sidekick in her first movie, and who has made one catastrophic mistake of his own after the other since then, not to mention harvesting Carol's DNA without permission and making it available to terrorists, thought at least The Marvels blatantly ignores all the Secret Invasion stuff). Or that one guy on the water planet ordering Monica to smile more which she immediately does. Or the female villain being an overtly emotional mess who backstabs people at a time when it brings her absolutely no benefit because, y'all know, women are irrational. Frankly Brie Larson should have gotten another Oscar for somehow selling all of this (the fact that I still like Carol and would love to see more of her is a testament to her acting skills). And the really sad thing is that The Marvels still isn't the worst movie the MCU have brought out in phase 4-6, not even by a long shot. (It even has what I would consider THE best scene in all the MCU movies, set to the soundtrack of "Memory". But that's wholly unrelated to its, and the MCU as a whole's, treatment of female characters.) I should have been clearer about that, sorry. Carol's reckless and angry (she's not the original Avenger for nothing ;-)) which, yes, are emotions. But she's not a typical MCU heroine who constantly worries about how her friends and family see her or who'd burn the world solely for her family. Carol's a "get the job done" person and while she often acts before thinking, again she does so because she's being provoked into anger. In that way she's akin to many masculine heroes. This worked perfectly fine in the first movie. However in The Marvels her lack of attachment to concepts like family - and again she WAS there for Maria and Monica even during a galaxy-wide crisis as much as she could, it's just that she wouldn't neglect her job and drop everything for them when that's what the writers expect from a "good" female character - is suddenly a problem. The movie ends with her "redeeming herself" by moving to Earth in order to play caretaker for Monica's empty house and I guess sometimes hang out with Kamala, effectively giving up her job for no good reason (but finally fitting into the "family always comes first" mould the writers prefer).

posts.text: Again I agree with the premise, just not that it was poor handling. They're angry and revenge filled in the immediate aftermath, yes, because a guy just killed half of all living things. But most of them aren't consumed by it- the early scenes post timeskip do a good job showing that. Cap and Widow can't move on, but they're not boiling with vengeance, they're trying to help other people get past it. Tony started a family and initially doesn't even want to try to bring everyone back. Clint is the only one who became consumed by vengeance, but it's comic-accurate and also makes sense for the character- he was the family man of the avengers, he got out, he retired, and then they all died in an event he wasn't even aware was happening until it was too late. I would say hulk and thor weren't handled as well, but Hulk's issues arguably stem from the fact that he should have been angrier instead of dabbing with adoring fans, and Thor... I mean, I think they were going for depression there? It definitely didn't work but I didn't get the sense he was filled with rage as much as sorrow. Beautifully written explanation of John's character, much better than I could have said it. The scene of him, after losing everything, welding that makeshift shield together in the garage is something that gets to the spirit of Cap and a Captain America legacy character more than anything Sam (or Bucky in any of the comics I read in his time as cap) have ever done. Back when the show first came out I thought it should have ended with them deciding that no one man can live up to steve rogers, and having Sam, Bucky, and John all carry on his legacy with none of them being specifically captain america. (Namewise you could keep USAgent, though I dislike the name so I'd rather go with his original comics pre-cap name of Patriot. Winter Soldier is fine too since it's already a reference to the American Revolution, and while Sam is the trickiest I think there's definitely something there either with an Eagle motif or just keeping Falcon) I think they've really been pushing an attempt to do a similar thing to that by constantly bringing up that Sam doesn't have serum, but it falls flat in two ways. The first is that his projects practically treat him as if he has the serum anyway in combat, and the second is that in the middle of his show the wakandans- who Sam doesn't really even have any connection to- just show up and given him a suit made of the same metal as his shield. If anything he has MORE raw power than Steve did while in the suit, not to mention he can fly and use the black panther kinetic shield blast. And of course, he's always treated as 100% in the right and with bucky/the wakandans/etc hyping him up. The writers want you to root for him as if he's an underdog but don't put any work into making him one. Also important to point out that Sam and Bucky - and to be fair to Sam, he does push back on this... a little bit....- were already talking about beating the tar out of John and stealing the shield before he kills the flag smasher. Which is a huge writing misstep, because it really just exacerbates their fight with John looking less like them taking the shield back from someone unworthy and more like two guys- one of them ostensibly a veteran counselor- taking advantage of a veteran's panic attack to jump him.

posts.text: This Victorian manor is my third attempt at making Creator set 31167 (Haunted House) into a proper enclosed building, and for this version there were no half measures taken in it's design. I went back and started at the beginning, adding a brand new fold-open back half, taller roof with attic space, along with a few other major tweaks. The color of the original set and my first rendition was sand green and my second version was tan, but for this version I decided to go with medium nougat, which presented it's own special challenges. (Luckily, the big hollow cylinder quarter parts existed at a reasonable price in this color, so I picked up enough for both outwardly-protruding portions of the building.) The roof was rather interesting to design, and required numerous changes to the floor below it during the design and build phases in order to work properly with the hinges and wall structure. This would have been made less complicated by the use of a part that doesn't exist (four 2x2x3 inverted corner slopes would have been nice!) but I made due without them. As for the automobile MOC, it is heavily modified from set 40532 - Vintage taxi, which is itself based on a French car (specifically a Citroen Traction Avant) from the mid-to-late 1930s. I have three of these cars built in LEGO so far, with this one being in the color dark orange. The front of the house by itself. The rear of the house with chimney flue, back door and rear protrusion. (I wasn't sure what these round tower-like things are called, so if somebody knows please enlighten me!) Inside the front of the house, with various furniture including (among others not listed): a couch, typewriter, organ, and a bookcase. The inside of the rear with it's bed, telephone, cuckoo clock, and safe. (The design of the safe is taken from Toy Story set 7594 - Woody's Roundup.) The front of the car with it's owner. This mini-figure also shows up in the first picture in the thread, as he owns the house too. I added the spare tire to this model as it was sorely missing from the original set. The car seats two figures inside and has room for some luggage at the extreme rear. Much like the real car, you can only get suitcases in or out by going over the back seat! That's all folks! Thanks for looking, and any thoughts are appreciated!

posts.text: Right. And sort of like renny mentions, there were ways to make this work. You could have them be robin hood types who are merely stealing the supplies (and also actually show us that they're being misallocated- as-is all we know about that is that the people who blew up the warehouse said it was) and not murdering people, and then at the end Sam's speech takes on the lens of you can't just throw money at the problem, you have to make sure it's getting to the people who need it. You could have it so the flag smashers DO act like they do in the show, and are just using the snap as an excuse to act out. But as is Sam is at best infantalizing the flag smashers and at worst actively defending a group that- despite what he says- are definitionally terrorists that murdered a bunch of innocents. Yeah. The classic example is batman and joker where Batman is actively complicit at this point, because it's been shown in plenty of continuities that joker is committing all these murders so he can have his playdates with batman. It's not necessarily batman's responsibility to kill him himself, but when somebody like red hood or punisher that one time or even presumably the gotham justice system wants to kill him, Bruce defending Joker is allowing those murders to continue. That doesn't mean heroes can't have no kill rules, but when they actively prevent others from killing the bad guy, it does paint them in a bad light. Red Goblin is a great arc, but when Peter stops JJJ from shooting Norman at the end, it's a little ridiculous. (Granted you have the slight wrinkle there that they're increasingly making the goblin a separate thing, but at the same time this isn't Raimi Norman who's a normal man with an alternate personality, this guy without any influence from the goblin invaded Asgard. He's been given enough slack.) I recently read the Devil's Trigger DD/Punisher story and I thought they handled it well there- Daredevil won't kill and doesn't like that Punisher does, but when they're in combat he's not going to go out of his way to stop him. When they get to the mastermind behind the story, Matt convinces Frank to let him live so the police can interrogate him to find others who were part of his network. Punisher forces Daredevil to reconcile with the fact that 90% of the mobsters they just fought were people Daredevil/Matt Murdock put away who were got out on bail years, months, days later, and they don't do any BS like "maybe they'll redeem themselves after murder #47", and Matt comes out of it obviously still with his rule but thinking that maybe Punisher needs to exist. Even with Loki- he's essentially just extradited to Asgard to face justice there. If Odin wanted to have him executed I doubt any of the avengers besides Thor would object. But is anybody out there saying that Carol "needs redemption" for that? Is anybody saying that she needs to be watching over an adult woman? Honestly I don't think I've even run into anyone blaming her for inadvertently decimating the Kree homeworld, but that may be a result of most people- especially those who weren't fans of Carol- not having watched the marvels. (and on the MCU as a whole for this butchering of the kree-skrull war that eliminates any nuance by making the kree the unilateral villains and the skrulls innocent.) At least in the comics, she's got a fairly similar personality to Tony- the difference being that Tony is constantly having to atone for his recklessness and in the MCU often spiraling deeper and deeper while attempting to do so. (And of course in the comics they just straight up character assassinated her by having her start another civil war, order the murder and/or jailing of multiple heroes based on things they might do, beat Tony into a coma and then just... forget to bring that up ever again. Though this is of course the era of hydra cap so it wasn't exactly good writing for any of the characters involved for a few years.)
